item.title: China Open Source Daily — 2026-11-19
item.description: Three documents this fortnight describe the same commercial turn of Chinese open source from three altitudes, and none of them is about code. Bank of Communications passed CAICT's trusted-open-source governance maturity assessment at the advanced grade on 2026-11-10, and the instrument that carried it there is a proprietary-governance practice, not an open-source one: a dual-repository split between 'new technology' and 'standardised technology', and an insistence that every open-source dependency retain a documented exit from the codebase. Moonshot AI, whose Kimi K3 is the largest open-weight model in the world, is unwinding its Cayman holding company and repapering its dollar investors into its mainland operating entity ahead of a Hong Kong listing, while its founder holds 51.83 per cent of that entity and the company's own disclosures show API revenue above seventy per cent with overseas users growing 400 per cent. And Zhipu, listed in Hong Kong since January, closed on 2026-11-17 at HK$335 with HK$163.5 billion of market value, down nearly ninety per cent from its June peak and down from a price-to-sales multiple above one thousand at the top. The open licence made the copy free. The three documents show that the copy was never where the value was — and that the vehicle now being built to own the value is a repo, a shareholder register and an API meter.
